rationale: A wins because it knows what it does not know and turns missing facts into reporting requirements instead of decorating the gap. Its competitive angle says "the user must supply names and dates — the fact block doesn't name them," while B prints "Apple Watch Has Had It for Years" and then asks someone else to confirm the year. B has sharper individual packaging in places, but it keeps spending facts it was not given; that is how a founder gets embarrassed on the first reporter callback.
gaps_in_A: "Cuffless blood pressure is the next wearable battleground" is a little loose because the supplied fact says the feature requires a one-time cuff calibration. The angle can survive, but the headline needs to stop implying the cuff disappears cleanly.
"the average wearer can't tell the difference" is plausible, but not supplied. Make it a question or support it with UI/disclaimer evidence.

"catch-up-and-leapfrog story" overreaches unless Whoop can prove the blood-pressure approach is meaningfully ahead. A mostly catches this with "claimed next edge," but the headline still wants restraint.
The first and fourth angles both lean on ECG parity plus blood pressure as the next front. They are different enough, but in a real campaign I would pick one after seeing validation data.
gaps_in_B: "Whoop Finally Has FDA-Cleared ECG. Apple Watch Has Had It for Years." Apple is not named in the update, and "for years" is not supplied. That is the cleanest unforced error in the set.
"a condition linked to stroke and heart failure" may be medically true, but it is not in the provided facts. In this exercise, that is imported seriousness, not grounding.
"Health Equity Story" is too heavy for the evidence given. A premium tier creates an access question; a health-equity angle needs price, demographics, availability, or affected populations.

"a deliberate regulatory positioning move" and "structured it to avoid diagnostic liability" state motive and legal strategy before the proof exists. The proof section knows this is unresolved; the angle copy should know it too.
